reconcile.connective: Gill limits Jesus's woe to praise purchased by compromise, distinguishing it from the good name Ecclesiastes and Proverbs praise.

discrepancy.connective: Daniel G. Taylor's BibViz Project (citing EvilBible.com) presses the point: Ecclesiastes and Proverbs praise a good name while Luke 6:26 curses universal praise.

skeptic.name: Daniel G. Taylor
skeptic.work: BibViz Project (Bible Contradictions Visualized), citing EvilBible.com
skeptic.attribution: Daniel G. Taylor, BibViz Project, "Is a good name a blessing or curse?" (bibviz.org, 2013), sourced from EvilBible.com

excerpts.excerpt_text: it is no bad sign, to have the good word of good men, and therefore these must be excepted, and the passage must be limited to bad men; for so did their fathers to the false prophets …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill directly reconciles the woe with the wisdom tradition's praise of a good name by limiting Luke 6:26's target to praise won from bad men, explicitly excepting the good word of good men as no bad sign.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-1763)
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: On Luke 6:25 Gill limits the woe to universal praise won from 'bad men,' explicitly excepting 'the good word of good men' -- the reputation Ecclesiastes 7:1 and Proverbs 22:1 commend.
